definition: A machine learning approach where models are trained across multiple devices or servers without sharing raw data, keeping personal information local while still enabling AI improvements.
metaDescription: Learn about federated learning - a privacy-preserving AI training method that keeps your data on your device while still improving machine learning models.
simpleExplanation: Instead of sending your personal data to a central server for AI training, federated learning allows your device to help train AI models locally. Only the learning insights are shared, not your actual data.
whyItMatters: Federated learning enables AI improvements while protecting privacy by keeping sensitive data on users' devices. This reduces privacy risks, complies with data protection laws, and builds user trust in AI systems.
technicalDetail: In federated learning, a global model is distributed to participating devices. Each device trains the model locally using its data, then sends only model updates (gradients or weights) back to a central server. The server aggregates these updates to improve the global model without ever accessing raw user data.

examples.explanation: Your phone learns from your typing patterns to improve autocorrect suggestions without sending your messages to Google or Apple servers.
Hospitals can collaboratively train AI models to detect diseases without sharing patient records, keeping sensitive health data within each institution.
Voice assistants can improve speech recognition by learning from all users while keeping individual conversations private and on-device.
